statement: scripts/run-classified-test-files.js dispatched every lane alphabetically in 100-file batches, so the long files of a parallel lane trailed a different batch each time and a previously red file waited its alphabetical turn. Each lane is now ordered from the last results (.tap/test-results/<file>.tap, the runner's top-level `# time=<ms>ms` tail): red, untimed or missing results first, then longest-first on a parallel lane and shortest-first on a serial lane (same total, earliest red). A fresh linked worktree (a quest, the push gate's corpus checkout) has no results and reads the main checkout's. Simulated on today's results with the runner's pull-queue: ordinary lane 418 s -> 312 s; serial lanes unchanged in total. Planning reads ~58 MB of results in ~200 ms warm. The set of every lane is unchanged; only order and batch composition change. test/shards/timings.json, which nothing reads, is retired. This also carries land-retry-parity's deferred 'previously red first'.

constraints.statement: Every lane holds exactly the files it held before; the plan's completeness and duplicate refusals are unchanged.
No readable result (CI, a plain fresh checkout) leaves every file unknown and the lane alphabetical, as before; a result never admits or drops a file.
The reader and ordering use captured intrinsics and the change-proof string collections, so the post-import collection replacement witness keeps delivering.
